book.title: In Search of Canadian Liberalism

argument.statement: Underhill’s evolving thought consistently searches for liberal values in Canada, positioning him as a political thinker whose minority views often anticipated later public opinion.

book.rationale: The book primarily explores Canadian liberalism within the context of political history, making Politics & Government the dominant subject.
book.summary: "Something in my heredity or in my environment," says Professor Underhill, "made it certain that I should never belong or want to belong to the Establishment." He cast his first vote in 1911, for Reciprocity, and thus began his long career of disagreeing with the majority of his fellow Canadians, His influence on them, however, has been far-reaching. As this remarkable selection of articles written by him over the past thirty years shows, he was usually a jump ahead of most of his contemporaries. By the time public opinion had caught up with his position of last year, he had moved on to a new one - equally shocking at first, at last commonly accepted. He is thus a rare example of the genuine leader of political thought. As such his stand was often lonely. But in his minority of one, good sense, style and a sharp wit have never deserted him. The essays here brought together are printed, except for a few minor changes to avoid repetition, exactly as they first appeared. They do not offer in any way a comprehensive study of the subject of liberalism in Canada. They mirror the mind of one man whose interests have tended to shift to and from between liberalism (with a small l) and Liberalism (with a capital L), and whose developing thought has always shown a lively consistency in its search for liberal values in Canada.
